To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lowering LDL-C by rosuvastain and atorvstatin could result in regression of coronary atheromatous plaque.
lowering LDL-C by statins therapy could lead to the reduction in the volume of coronary atherosclerosis plaques.
intensive lowering of LDL-C with statins therapy could lead to the reduction of coronary atherosclerosis plaques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of LDL cholesterol on the progression of coronary atherosclerosis, and provides evidence for clinical practice and research.
the effects of lowering LDL-C on CAP regression, but not the effects of lowering triglyceride or non-HDL-C on the volume of CAP.
the relationship between LDL-C level and CAP regression, which is a significant step in the prevention of coronary heart disease and the treatment of coronary atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

lowering LDL-C to a level <78.0 mg/dL with rosuvastatin mean dose 33 mg or atorvastain mean dose 60 mg for ≥ 17 months would lead to the regression or stabilization of CAP in patients with coronary atherosclerosis.
lowering LDL-C level by >40% with statins could result in the regression of CAP in patients with coronary artery disease.
the target level of lowering LDL-C for regressing CAP should be >40% or LDL-C <78 mmol/L.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lowering LDL-C to a target level of <78 mmol/L (3.0 mg/dL) could result in regression of coronary atheroma.
intensive statin therapy with LDL-C lowering by >40% could lead to regression of CAP.
the LDL-C lowering treatment should aim at a target level ≤ 80 mg/dL to achieve the regression of the CAP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the target level of lowering LDL-C for regressing CAP is not 100 mg/dL.
LDL-C lowering therapy can significantly reduce the volume CAP, and the regression of CAP can be achieved when the LDL-C level is reduced by >40%.
LDL-C levels and LDL-C lowering therapy have a dose-response effect on the regression of CAP.
